title: Hunting for 3rds
summary: Find the major and minor 3rds anywhere on the neck, then see how Trey Anastasio uses them. Under the jam-band Mixolydian sound, he plays like a blues player. Type in any chord progression and the lesson maps the 3rds, the shortest route between them and drills for each change.
description: Learn where major and minor 3rds sit on the guitar neck, then type any chord progression to see the 3rds, the shortest route between them and Trey Anastasio style drills.
intro: The 3rd is the note that makes a chord sound major or minor. Hit it when the chord changes and your solo follows the song, even if you never look at a chart. This lesson shows where every 3rd sits on the neck, then rebuilds itself around whatever progression you type.

Most people hear Trey Anastasio and think jam band, Mixolydian, long open-ended solos. Underneath all that he plays like a blues guitarist. He knows the chord, finds its 3rd and builds the phrase from there. This lesson looks at how he goes after each change.
